I think this is somewhat taking things out of context. One of the big reason Google started lobbying hard is that Microsoft was using their bought politicians to try to put legal and political pressure on Google. Google responded by buying their own politicians. Apparently they liked the result. 2007, the year their lobbying spiked, was -along with a number of spurious antitrust investigations- also the year that the FTC decided to prevent Google from acquiring DoubleClick - some random ad company because they argued it would be anti competitive. This is the same FTC that had been happily condoning all sorts of anti competitive behaviors and mergers from Comcast / Time Warner / and so on. The FTC changed their mind.... for some reason... and agreed to the acquisition in 2008.

The article mentions Google spending $16.7 million in lobbying in 2015. That can buy you an incredible amount of unfair treatment in the US - but it can also similarly buys you protection from unfair treatment against yourself. And perhaps most importantly that $16.7 million is exactly 0.02% of their 2015 revenue. If you earn $30,000 a year then that's the equivalent of $6 for an all you can eat buffet of US politiicans. Politicians, relative to the profits of huge companies, cost table scraps.

I think focusing on Google in this situation is disingenuous. They only started playing the corruption game when politicians forced them to at the beckoning of other corporations pulling their strings. The problem is not Google, the problem is politicians who will do damned near anything for more 'donations' as those are essentially what keep them in office and have become little more than a euphemism for bribes when sufficient in size. In many ways our system has changed from one where a politician's job is to represent the people to one where a politician's job is to solicit donations. In our elections the one and only thing that correlates strongly with success is money spent on a campaign. It's broken.

Does anyone else remember "Don't be evil"? Seems so long ago that Google was worth a damn as a company. Don't really use any of their products anymore. To be frank, they never really innovated anything that stuck. There are other search engines, e-mail services and GPS systems to use that aren't nearly as creepy as Google's.
